title: Slow computer & freezes
blurb: Slow, frozen, fan loud, high CPU or memory, apps not responding.

remedies.title: Antivirus scan slows everything down
remedies.why: A full scan or real-time scanning of many files (builds, sync folders) uses a lot of disk and CPU.

steps.text: Let a running scan finish, or schedule full scans for when you're away.
Two antivirus products at once slow everything; keep one.
Don't turn protection off; ask IT about excluding big development or sync folders.

remedies.title: "kernel_task" or "WindowServer" uses lots of CPU on a Mac
remedies.why: kernel_task takes CPU on purpose to cool a hot Mac; WindowServer gets busy with many screens, windows or effects.

steps.text: Let the Mac cool: hard surface, unblocked vents, unplug a hot charger for a moment.
Close windows and apps you aren't using; fewer external displays help WindowServer.
Turn on Reduce Motion and Reduce Transparency in Accessibility › Display.
Watch it in Activity Monitor.

remedies.title: Indexing (SearchIndexer / mds) keeps the computer busy
remedies.why: After big changes (new computer, update, lots of new files) search indexing runs for hours, then calms down.

steps.text: Leave the computer on and plugged in for a few hours to let indexing finish.
If it never stops, rebuild the index.
Exclude big folders you never search (Spotlight Privacy).

remedies.title: Lots of apps run in the background
remedies.why: Updaters, sync tools and helpers start with the computer and keep running.

steps.text: Quit tray icons you don't need, then stop them starting.
Turn off background items you don't recognise in Login Items & Extensions.
Uninstall trial antivirus and "PC optimizers" that came with the computer.

remedies.title: Games or graphics apps run slowly
remedies.why: The app runs on the power-saving graphics chip, the driver is old, or the laptop is on battery saver.

steps.text: Plug in and choose Best performance.
Settings › System › Display › Graphics: set the game to High performance.
Update the graphics driver from NVIDIA/AMD/Intel.
Turn on Game Mode.
Turn off Low Power Mode; lower the game's resolution.

remedies.title: Is it time to upgrade or replace my computer?
remedies.why: Most slowness on older PCs comes from a spinning hard disk or too little memory, both often fixable.

steps.text: Check memory and disk type: Task Manager › Performance (Memory, Disk type SSD/HDD).
System Information shows memory and storage.
Windows PCs: an SSD and 16 GB memory revive most machines from the last ~8 years.
Macs can't be upgraded inside; Apple silicon Macs stay fast for many years.

remedies.title: Spinning beach ball all the time
remedies.why: An app is waiting (on disk, network or memory). Often full storage or memory pressure.

steps.text: Check free storage (keep 20 GB+ free).
Check Memory Pressure and which app is "Not Responding" in Activity Monitor.
Restart; update macOS and the app.
